findings.title: Invalid `end if` makes the embed template fail to compile
findings.body: Line 6 closes the header `if` with `end if` and no condition. ERB compiles this to Ruby containing `end if`, which is a SyntaxError, so every request that renders `embed/best` will raise instead of displaying discussion highlights or the start-discussion link. It should just be `<%- end %>`. Controller specs do not render views by default, so this is not caught.

findings.title: Imported feed/readability HTML is stored as raw HTML and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns the raw string for that method, bypassing Markdown/sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds arbitrary RSS/Atom content here (after `CGI.unescapeHTML`, which can turn escaped `<script>` into a real script tag), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` emits `raw post.cooked`. The readability path only filters tag/attribute names, not dangerous URL schemes, and line 13 interpolates the feed-provided URL unescaped into the raw post. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject script/event-handler HTML and execute it in the forum origin when the embed is viewed. Sanitize the HTML (and URL schemes/attributes) before storing it, or do not use the raw_html cook method for untrusted feed content.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL instead of an origin
findings.body: The resize script sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `targetOrigin` must be a serialized origin (scheme://host[:port]); a referer with a path (and query string, which ERB also HTML-escapes to `&` inside the script) does not match the parent origin. The browser therefore drops the message, so the iframe never receives the height and content is clipped to the initial iframe size. Build the target origin from `URI(request.referer).scheme`, host, and port (or use a controlled site setting), not the full URL.

findings.title: Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort polling
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` field. Many valid feeds provide only `description` or `summary`, so `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises, aborting the entire poll and preventing all later items from importing. Use `i.content || i.description` (and handle nil) before scrubbing/unescaping.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin equality
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;` accepts any origin that appears as a substring of the trusted URL, for example `http://forum.example` when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com`, or the same host on a different port. Such a page can send a `discourse-resize` message and control the iframe height. Compare `e.origin` against the normalized origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

findings.title: Guard tests pass without exercising the setting under test
findings.body: The `feed_polling_url` test stubs only `feed_polling_url` to nil; it leaves `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default false, so `execute` short-circuits before the URL check. The `embed_by_username` test has the same issue. These tests would still pass if the corresponding condition were deleted. Stub all earlier guards true in each test, and only the condition under test false, to make the assertion meaningful.

findings.title: URL absolutization corrupts protocol-relative URLs and misses path-relative URLs
findings.body: Only root-relative links are rewritten, and protocol-relative URLs are corrupted: `//cdn.example.com/x` satisfies `start_with?('/')`, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/x` instead of `http://cdn.example.com/x`. Path-relative URLs such as `foo/bar` are not absolutized at all. The same issue exists for `img[src]` below. Treat `//` separately and resolve relative URLs against the article URI.

findings.title: Unvalidated `open(url)` allows command execution/file reads from Disqus links
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation. Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats a string beginning with `|` as a shell command and other strings as local file paths, so a malicious Disqus export can put e.g. `|touch /tmp/pwned` or `/etc/passwd` in a thread link; `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` now passes `t[:link]` directly to this method. Running the importer would execute the command or read the file. Validate that the URL is http/https and use an HTTP client (with redirect/size/timeout handling) instead of Kernel#open.
